name: British Virgin Islands
summary: A Dutch foothold on Tortola becomes a lasting English possession.
notes: The main track follows Tortola. The timing and extent of authority over the other islands differed; a modern archipelago should not be projected intact into the seventeenth century.

events.title: A Spanish claim to the Virgin Islands
events.detail: The Spanish expedition named the group; durable Spanish settlement did not follow.
events.qualification: A European claim; it does not establish island-wide administration or extinguish Indigenous rights.

events.title: Informal Dutch settlement
events.detail: Joost van Dyk and other settlers operated on Tortola before a formal colony.
events.uncertainty: Settlement chronology is approximate and the early communities were politically fluid.

events.title: A Dutch colony on Tortola
events.detail: Dutch settlement acquired a more organized colonial form.

events.title: English occupation
events.detail: The Second Anglo-Dutch War brought a brief English interruption.

events.title: England takes Tortola
events.detail: The English governor described a conquest; the Dutch later described a protective arrangement and sought restitution.

events.title: The English claim prevails
events.detail: Diplomatic negotiations failed to restore Dutch administration; British possession endured.
events.uncertainty: There was no single unambiguous cession date. This is a conventional endpoint for the late-century dispute.

events.title: A separate British colony
events.detail: Administrative separation from the Leeward Islands did not constitute independence.
